meta.title: Doesn't revalidate project files after classpath changes if autobuild is off.
meta.fix_ref: bb26c98d (Revalidate open files in project when classpath updates.), 2024-05-16; git tag --contains: first in v1.37.0
meta.build_notes: Eclipse JDT LS release tarballs 1.36.0 (jdt-language-server-1.36.0-202405301306) and 1.37.0 (-202406271335), unpacked under temp/lsp_servers/ and run on the bundled JDK 17 with a private -data directory per session. The first session resolves the Maven dependency (commons-lang3 3.5) and the compiler plugin into ~/.m2/repository.
meta.notes: Converted from the validated state-bug spike (scripts/lsp_repro/cases/jdtls_3155.py), but with the reporter's own reproduction instead of the spike's hand-made .classpath project: the Maven project 'salut' from the issue (pom.xml and Foo.java verbatim) and the reported steps (delete the dependency from the open pom.xml, save; the build file change reaches the server as a watched-file change, as the editor's file watcher reports the save). Not in candidates.jsonl (JDT LS was not part of the candidate mining).

settings_note: java.autobuild.enabled=false is the precondition named in the issue title; java.configuration.updateBuildConfiguration=automatic (session default) stands for the reporter answering yes to the synchronize prompt.

repro.steps: With java.autobuild.enabled=false: open Foo.java and pom.xml and let the server settle (step 1). Delete the commons-lang3 dependency from pom.xml and save it; the configuration update is automatic in the session settings (the reporter clicked yes on 'synchronize the Java classpath'), and the saved build file reaches the server as a watched-file change, as the editor's file watcher reports it (step 2). Reported: no errors appear in Foo.java because its diagnostics are stale; they appear only once the file gets focus (step 3). Probe (R1): the diagnostics of Foo.java must equal those of a fresh session on the final files (which reports the unresolved import and StringUtils).
